reason: Every measurement in this finding checks out when driven, and the fix delivers exactly what it claims. Driven in chromium at 320/360/390/414/768/1280/1440, light and dark, all seven states, measuring the last .coverage span with a Range over its contents so the line boxes are read rather than inferred. The stamp's unwrapped width is 349.2px (identical at 414, 768, 1280 and 1440, where it sets on one line). At 390 the .coverage content box is exactly 342px, so the stamp overflows by 7.2px and wraps to two lines: line one runs 24 -> 358 and ends after 'THE', and line two is a single client rect 7.6px wide at x=24. 7.6px is exactly one glyph of 11px Geist Mono at 0.99px tracking (the 33-character READ stamp measures 250.5px, 7.59px/char), so the second line is the bare digit 9 and nothing else. The element screenshot of .coverage at 390 confirms it: 'BOUND WORKSPACE, OWNER, READING DATE AND THE' then '9' alone. It reproduces in full, partial, quiet, first-run, empty, loading and error at 390, and in the dark twin; it clears at 414 and above, so 390 and 360 are the exposed widths (at 360 the widow is 'THE 9', at 320 'AND THE 9' plus the Lab stamp also wraps). The code reading is right too: .coverage at lately.html:505 is a wrapping flex container with no white-space or hyphenation control and the stamps carry no internal break control, so the break point is whatever falls out of the measure. The gate observation at interaction-check.mjs:259-267 is also right and is the more valuable half: the comment claims both halves are 'short enough for the stamp voice it is set in' and cites the 134-character string that ran too long, but the assertion beneath it is only /lab-authored/ && /Bound/ && /reading date/ on textContent - three presence tests. Nothing in either gate measures a stamp's set width against its container, which is why a stamp that no longer fits its own measure passes green. This is not the round-2 'bound-nine-prints-where-no-nine-was-read' claim: that was refuted on what the nine asserts, this is where the line breaks, and the two share no mechanism. Severity: the seat classed this refinement, which is understated by one class - refinement means nothing is wrong, and a one-character widow at the primary mobile width is visibly wrong, if passable. It is a defect at the mild end: nothing is misstated, no number is wrong, the provenance strip simply breaks its own sentence one character short at the width the surface ships to a phone.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix as proposed - in shell() at lately.html:956, 'Bound workspace, owner, reading date and the ${D.open}'. Simulated in the live DOM at 390 it does what it says: the break moves to after 'DATE', line two becomes 68.3px = 'AND THE 9', the span stays two lines at 29.69px and the strip stays 122.06px, so nothing below moves and no horizontal overflow appears (documentElement.scrollWidth stays 390, and 360 and 320 stay clean too). The gate's three substring tests still pass, because the two non-breaking spaces sit between 'and'/'the' and 'the'/'9' and never inside 'reading date'. Do not reach for white-space: nowrap on .coverage span instead - at 390 the stamp is 7.2px wider than its 342px container, so nowrap converts a wrap into an overflow. While the file is open, close the hole the finding actually found by making the gate able to fail: after the existing coverage assertions, assert at 390 that no .coverage span's last line box is narrower than two glyphs - e.g. for each span take Array.from(document.createRange() over its contents .getClientRects()), group by rounded top, and require the last group's total width > 16px. That is the assertion the comment at line 259 has been describing without testing since it was written.
breaks: Nothing structural, but three things to re-measure after it lands. (1) The strip's set copy is now break-controlled in one stamp and not in the other five - re-run the same last-line measurement across all six stamps at 320/360/390 in every state, because the empty and error states carry longer source stamps ('Tasks answered, nothing recorded' is 242.9px) and the partial state's 'Timeline did not answer' reflows the first row. (2) The nbsp is inside a template literal that is not passed through esc(), so it must stay a literal   entity in the HTML string; if anyone later routes that stamp through esc() the entity will print as visible text - assert on textContent containing '\u00a0', not on the entity source. (3) Re-shoot light-full--390x844.png and the dark twin: the current committed 390 frame is the one showing the stranded digit, and leaving it in shots/ leaves the defect in the record after it is fixed. Height does not change, so no other frame needs re-capture.
